title: Incident-bot: require incident_type/subtype + auto-resolve owner before resolve/close
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
description:
Goal
Make incident classification mandatory and auditable by enforcing incident_type + incident_subtype selection in incident-bot, resolving a primary owner team from a lookup table, and preventing incidents from being marked Resolved/Closed without required fields.

Why
Taxonomy + ownership mapping is the backbone for reporting (volume by type/owner, MTTR, SLA compliance) and for consistent on-call behavior. Today we have too many incidents that end with freeform tags and unclear owner attribution, which makes trending and accountability difficult.

Scope
1) Required fields in incident creation + update flows
- Add required incident_type and incident_subtype fields to the Slack modal used by /incident start and incident-bot shortcuts.
- For existing open incidents, require setting missing fields before allowing transition to Resolved/Closed.
- Provide an explicit "Unknown / Needs triage" option that is allowed only during active response, but must be replaced with a specific type/subtype before close.

2) Owner resolution
- Given (incident_type, incident_subtype), auto-resolve:
  - owner_team (primary)
  - escalation_channel (e.g., #eng-routing-oncall)
  - optional runbook link suggestions
- Owner mapping source of truth:
  - v1: static allowlist JSON in incident-bot repo (fast path for rollout)
  - follow-up: switch to Control Plane managed mapping (ENG-4825) once available; keep a safe fallback to the last-known-good config.

3) Validation + closure gating
- Block "Resolve" and "Close" actions unless:
  - incident_type is set
  - incident_subtype is set (or explicitly "none" when allowed by type)
  - owner_team is resolved (or manually set by IC with a reason if mapping is missing)
- For Sev0/Sev1: also require a postmortem link or placeholder ticket (tracked separately; incident-bot already has partial support—ensure this ticket does not regress that behavior).

4) Auditing + analytics
- Emit a structured event when taxonomy is set/changed:
  - who changed it (Slack user)
  - timestamp
  - previous -> new type/subtype
  - owner_team at time of change
- Add counters for:
  - % incidents created with Unknown
  - time-to-classification (Unknown -> classified)
  - mapping misses (type/subtype not found)

Non-goals
- Designing the taxonomy itself (ENG-4821)
- Pager routing updates based on incident_type (ENG-4823)
- Auto-suggestion heuristics (separate PR; tracked in incident-bot PR-826)

Acceptance criteria
- Cannot resolve/close an incident without incident_type/subtype + owner_team present.
- "Unknown" is selectable at incident start, but cannot be present at Close.
- Mapping misses are surfaced clearly in Slack (with a link to request a mapping update) and do not silently default to SRE.
- Backwards compatible: existing incident links, channel topics, and incident summaries continue to work.
- Clear admin escape hatch for force majeure / tooling failures, with audit logging.

Implementation notes
- Taxonomy values must be low-cardinality and match the Confluence v1 allowlist (no freeform strings).
- Store canonical keys in incident-bot state (e.g., "routing.fallback_misbehavior") and render friendly names in Slack UI.
- Keep Slack modal within platform limits: use a top-level dropdown for incident_type, and a dependent dropdown for incident_subtype.
- Manual override flow:
  - If mapping not found, let IC set owner_team from a dropdown of on-call teams and require a short reason (1–2 sentences).

Rollout plan
- Phase 1 (internal-only): enable required fields for SRE + Platform workspaces; monitor mapping miss rate.
- Phase 2: enable for all eng workspaces; announce in #eng-sre.
- Phase 3: enforce closure gating globally; remove temporary bypass after 2 weeks.

comments: 2025-12-06 (Devon Price): Drafted Slack modal changes locally. Slack UI constraint: dependent dropdowns require a modal update on type selection; implementing as: select type -> submit "Next" -> reopen modal with subtype choices. Slightly clunky but stays within Slack constraints. Alternative is a single combined "type / subtype" dropdown; keeping as fallback.

2025-12-08 (Allison Grant): Please ensure taxonomy keys are strict allowlist. No freeform strings. Also add a distinct bucket for "unknown" rather than nulls; we need to measure how often people hit it.

2025-12-09 (Dylan Brooks): Closure gating must cover both "Resolved" and "Closed" transitions. We’ve had incidents where folks skip resolve and close directly. Add audit log event for any bypass/override.

2025-12-11 (Ethan Park): ENG-4825 will provide the control-plane mapping but won’t land before end of month. OK to ship a static v1 mapping file first. Please structure it so we can swap the backing store later without changing incident state schema.

2025-12-14 (Rafael Mendes): Confirmed policy: "Unknown" is permitted at creation, but not at closure. If still unknown at close, treat as process failure; bot should explicitly block and message: "Select the best-fit primary type; add contributing factors in postmortem."

2025-12-18 (Devon Price): Implemented mapping miss flow. If (type, subtype) missing, bot prompts IC to pick owner_team from allowlist of on-call teams + requires a reason. Logged as "owner_override=true" for reporting.

2026-01-03 (Dev Patel): From Support POV, we need owner_team to resolve to the team Slack channel (not just "Routing"). Please include escalation_channel in bot summary so Support can join the right place quickly.

2026-01-07 (Devon Price): PR up: incident-bot#812. Includes required fields + owner resolution + gating. Added metrics counters: incident_created_unknown, incident_closed_unknown_blocked, owner_mapping_miss, owner_override_used.

2026-01-10 (Rafael Mendes): Tested in #incidents-sandbox. Gating works. One UX snag: users creating incident via shortcut now have a two-step modal flow. Acceptable for v1; we’ll rely on auto-suggest (PR-826) to reduce friction.
2026-01-14 (Dylan Brooks): Approved with follow-ups: (1) add a link in the block message to the decision tree doc; (2) ensure the override path pings #eng-sre for visibility if used on Sev0/Sev1.
